description:
The same WHEN OTHER arm of EVALUATE EIBAID at app/cbl/COADM01C.cbl:99-102 that case18 pins, driven from a second and structurally different class of key: DFHCLEAR. The pair exists to separate two things one case cannot tell apart. Order is behaviour and WHEN OTHER must stay last (G30), but that only means something if the arm really is the ordered default rather than a fourth named key, and a single case reaching it proves only that the one byte it carried happened to have no arm of its own. So case18 sends a program-function key - DFHPF12, which common.CicsAid gives 0x7C - and this case sends a screen-clear key - DFHCLEAR, 0x6D - which is not a function key at all: a different key class on the 3270, from a different byte range, reached by a different physical key. Both are required to produce the identical outcome, and that is the AID-independence the arm claims: :100 to :102 never read EIBAID again, so once the byte is neither DFHENTER's 0x7D nor DFHPF3's 0xF3 the outcome cannot depend on which byte it was. DFHPA1 at 0x6C would serve as a third class if a further case ever needed one. Everything below apart from the AID is byte-identical to case18 deliberately - that identity IS the assertion - so a divergence between the two files is a defect in one of them rather than a difference between two paths.

Two dispatch mechanisms exist in this migration and this case turns on not conflating them. COADM01C tests EIBAID inline and its own EVALUATE has a WHEN OTHER: the COPY list at :50-61 is COCOM01Y, COADM02Y, COADM01, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA, CSSTRPFY is not among them, and :93 therefore compares the raw byte against two named mnemonics with a third and last arm catching everything else. common.PfKeyResolver is the other mechanism: it reproduces app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy's EIBAID-to-five-character-token mapping, whose EVALUATE TRUE carries 28 arms and neither a WHEN OTHER nor a DFHPA3 branch - which is exactly why the resolver represents a no-match as an explicit empty Optional rather than inventing a NONE token CVCRD01Y does not define. DFHCLEAR is the sharpest illustration available of why the two must not be confused, because CSSTRPFY does have an arm for it at :24-25 setting CCARD-AID-CLEAR, so PfKeyResolver.resolve maps this very byte to a real token, AidKey.CLEAR with the literal 'CLEAR'. Resolvability is nevertheless irrelevant here, because COADM01C never asks. A translation that chose the arm by resolved token instead of by byte would be wrong in both directions at once: it would make PF15 behave as PF3, since the copybook folds both onto PFK03, and it would invite treating a resolvable key such as this one as though it had an arm of its own. The service compares bytes through PfKeyResolver.isAid for that reason, and leaves every byte but the two named ones on :99.

The arm does three things and this case pins all three. :100 MOVE 'Y' TO WS-ERR-FLG turns the error flag on. :101 MOVE CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY TO WS-MESSAGE loads the message, and its bytes are derived rather than transcribed: app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:20-21 declares CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY PIC X(50) from a 49-character source literal, which is 40 characters of text followed by 9 spaces, so the VALUE right-pads it by one to the field's 50. Moving that PIC X(50) sender into the PIC X(80) WS-MESSAGE of :38 left-justifies and space-fills the remaining 30, so the eighty-byte image below is the 40-character text 'Invalid key pressed. Please see below...' followed by exactly 40 spaces, and it is declared on the WS_MESSAGE_80 channel for that reason. The 78-byte ERRMSGO that :177 narrows it into - PIC X(78) at app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY:260 - is a different channel and the controller's step, not a different rounding of this one. Neither thank-you literal belongs anywhere near this case, and they are two literals rather than one: SystemMessages.CCDA_MSG_THANK_YOU is the PIC X(50) 'Thank you for using CardDemo application...' of CSMSG01Y, while ScreenTitles.CCDA_THANK_YOU is the PIC X(40) 'Thank you for using CCDA application...' of COTTL01Y - different texts at different widths owned by different copybooks. :102 PERFORM SEND-MENU-SCREEN is the third thing, so the screen IS repainted: :175 BUILD-MENU-OPTIONS recomposes the four active lines rather than echoing them, each one :231's MOVE SPACES followed by :233-236's STRING of the PIC 9(02) option number, the two-character '. ' literal and the PIC X(35) name - 2 plus 2 plus 35 is 39, and because STRING does not pad, the fortieth character is the space :231 left there - and :179-184 sends map COADM1A of mapset COADM01 with ERASE.

Four things the arm does not do are pinned as deliberately as the three it does. It performs no output reset. MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COADM1AO at :89 sits inside the IF NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER of :87 and is first-entry only, so on this REENTER half of gate G38 not one output field is cleared; OPTN005O to OPTN012O below are the unpainted image at their declared PIC X(40) because :228-229 iterates only to CDEMO-ADMIN-OPT-COUNT, which app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy fixes at 4, so lines 5 to 12 are never written at all rather than written and then blanked. It writes no colour: the only attribute byte COADM01C ever moves is the DFHGREEN of :148, on the coming-soon path this case never reaches, so ERRMSGC below is the mapset's own declared COLOR=RED at app/bms/COADM01.bms:154-157, named by its BmsAttributes.DFHRED mnemonic rather than a raw byte because colour is how this program distinguishes an error from a confirmation. There is no asterisk and no explicit DFHRED move, and there cannot be - CSSETATY is not in the COPY list, its only consumer in this migration is COACTUPC, and DFHRED appears zero times in the program's 268 lines - so expecting the CSSETATY highlight that G38 is usually phrased around would be inventing behaviour. It reads no option: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY is not performed on this arm, so :117-125 never run and :125's MOVE WS-OPTION TO OPTIONO never fires, which is why OPTIONO below is the '1 ' the client re-supplied and emphatically not the '01' the normalisation of :123 would have produced had the ENTER arm been taken. And it mutates no communication-area field: :100 to :102 touch working storage and the map only, :88's SET CDEMO-PGM-REENTER belongs to the first-entry branch this path did not take and :141's MOVE ZEROS TO CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT to the transfer branch it also did not take, so CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives 1 and leaves 1 and all sixteen fields of the 160-byte area round-trip identically. That the area is comparable at all is the whole of G37 - the conversation state travels in the payload and no server-side session holds it - and the transaction ends at :107-110's EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CA00') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), RETURN_TRANSID, with no successor named, which is why nextProgram is absent rather than blank.

The unit is AdminMenuService, constructed and called directly as a plain Java object with no HTTP and no MockMvc anywhere in the path (G51), and it is dispatched to the single-invocation service adapter rather than case18's three-run statelessness adapter: one invocation is all this case needs, because what it contributes to the pair is a second AID class and not a second execution shape. The thirteen items below are precisely what that service produces - the twelve menu lines and the option echo. TRNNAMEO, PGMNAMEO, TITLE01O, TITLE02O, CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are absent by design, because POPULATE-HEADER-INFO reads FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :204 and belongs to the controller if the service is to stay deterministic, and ERRMSGO is absent because the eighty-to-seventy-eight narrowing of :177 is the controller's step too. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the instant COADM01C's own version footer at :267 carries, so one clock governs every case in this directory, and US-ASCII is named explicitly rather than left to a platform default. Every expected value above is statically derived: read out of the COBOL paragraph that produces it and cross-checked against app/cbl/COADM01C.cbl, the PIC X(50) VALUE of app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy, the option table of app/cpy/COADM02Y.cpy, the xxxI and xxxO PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY and the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COADM01.bms. None of it was captured from, recorded against or replayed from an execution of the legacy program. There is no COBOL execution baseline behind it: none was produced, and none could be produced in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from this repository, which is precisely why the AID and attribute mnemonics this case names come from common.CicsAid and common.BmsAttributes. Only the provenance of the expected values changes; the twenty cases per program, the field-for-field comparison and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand unchanged. Because provenance is a stated success criterion, the substitution is escalated for explicit user confirmation rather than silently absorbed - risk R-A, as ParityHarness's class documentation states it.
